newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU bag sellers slam Commission's anti-dumping move.
newsitem.headline: EU bag sellers slam Commission's anti-dumping move.

text.p: European importers of luggage and sports bags criticised the European Commission on Friday for starting an anti-dumping probe into the EU's imports of various types of Chinese-made bags.
"In terms of European employment this will be counter productive to what the European Commission is aiming for with the anti-dumping duties," the Foreign Trade Association said in a statement.

"If the proceedings are approved, the consequences for European leather goods retail shops will be tremendous. It can be expected that 40 percent of their turnover will be lost and many of them will not survive," the FTA said at a news conference.
It was supported by a variety of European associations representing the sports goods, luggage, leather goods and accessories industries.
The Commission's inquiry, announced last April after complaints submitted by the European Committee for Leather Goods Industries, is due for a decision in the coming days, the FTA said.

The FTA said the products under scrutiny, essentially luggage and travel goods, briefcases, school bags and handbags made in China, were not manufactured in the European Union and so were not threatening any EU-based production.

"The concerned goods produced in China and in the European Union are basically different, they are complementary and seldom in competition. There is practically no EU production left for articles similar to Chinese products," it said.
The European Commission refused to comment on the remarks, saying only that an announcement could be expected once the inquiry was over.
